Batumi Boulevard and Old Town

A seven-kilometre seafront promenade, a nineteenth-century old quarter and modern towers in one compact city.

Time needed
6 h
From Tbilisi
370 km · 5:30
Road
Paved
Car needed
Economy class
Season
All year
Entry
free

Batumi is the capital of Adjara and the main city on Georgia's Black Sea coast. Seeing it divides neatly into two parts that lie about ten minutes' walk apart.

The first is the Boulevard. Laid out in the 1880s, it now runs for more than seven kilometres: pebble beach on one side, avenues, cycle paths, fountains and sculptures on the other. Its most famous fixture is the moving sculpture Ali and Nino, whose two figures pass through each other every evening. Nearby stand the Alphabet Tower and the cluster of modern high-rises that has completely rewritten the city skyline over the past two decades.

The second is the old town. In the late nineteenth century Batumi was a port and a free-trade centre, and the architecture reflects that: two- and three-storey buildings with deep balconies, the Piazza square, an astronomical clock and narrow streets full of cafes.

One thing to know in advance: Adjara is the wettest region in Georgia. Batumi receives roughly two and a half thousand millimetres of rain a year, and downpours are entirely possible in July and August. A three-day visit is often interrupted by one wet day. This is not a guaranteed-sunshine resort, and it is better to plan around that than be surprised by it.

Practical advice

Driving in the centre in summer is inefficient: parking is expensive and often full. Leave the car at your hotel and use the boulevard on foot or by rented bicycle. Evening is the best time on the promenade, when the heat drops and the fountains run. Rain is likely in any month, so keep an umbrella or a light shell in your bag rather than in the boot. ATMs, pharmacies and cafes are everywhere, and card payment is not a problem in the centre.

How to get there from Tbilisi

Tbilisi to Batumi is 370 km and about five and a half hours on the best road in the country. Follow the E60 through Gori, Khashuri, the new Rikoti tunnel section, Kutaisi and Samtredia, then drop down to the coast and enter Batumi past Kobuleti. The whole route is paved and much of it is dual carriageway, so an economy car is entirely sufficient. Fuel is available everywhere along the way. On summer weekends set off early, as coastal traffic backs up from mid-morning onward.

Nearby places

Nature

Batumi Botanical Garden

Over a hundred hectares on a cape above the sea, with nine floristic zones of the world laid out side by side.

Fortress

Gonio-Apsaros Fortress

A Roman military fort south of Batumi — 18 towers, active excavations and a grave traditionally linked to an apostle.

Fortress

Petra Fortress, Tsikhisdziri

Byzantine fortress ruins on a rocky headland above the sea, between Kobuleti and Batumi.
